options: The turn between two rays sharing an endpoint
questions.explanation: An angle is the amount of turn between two rays that share a vertex.
questions.misconception: A three-sided shape is a triangle, an endless path is a line, and a dot is a point — an angle is an open turn between rays.

questions.prompt: How many degrees are in a full turn around a point?
questions.explanation: A full circle around a point measures 360 degrees.
questions.misconception: A half turn is 180° and a quarter turn is 90° — only the complete circle back to the start is 360°.

questions.explanation: Angles smaller than 90° are acute; 25° is acute.
questions.misconception: Right means exactly 90°, and obtuse means bigger than 90° — any sharp turn under 90° is acute.

questions.prompt: What tool do you use to measure an angle?
questions.explanation: A protractor reads the degrees between the two rays.
questions.misconception: A ruler measures straight lengths, not turns — angles need a protractor's half-circle scale.

questions.prompt: The three angles of any triangle add up to...
questions.explanation: The three interior angles of a triangle always sum to 180°.
questions.misconception: A full turn is 360° and a single right angle is 90° — for a triangle the total is exactly 180°.
